references.text: The previous verse explains why the place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (graves of craving), because the people who had craved were buried there.
The route from Kibroth-hattaavah to Hazor is confirmed in the list of Israel's camp locations in the wilderness.
Kibroth-hattaavah is mentioned as a place where Israel provoked the Lord to anger, recalling the events that led to its naming.
The next chapter continues the story while the people are at Hazor, where Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses.
Describes the departure from Hazor after Miriam was healed, showing the further journey from this place.
